'''Pietro De Camilli''' [[National Academy of Sciences|NAS]], [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences|AAA&S]], [[National Academy of Medicine|NAM]] is an Italian-American biologist and John Klingenstein Professor of [[Neuroscience]] and [[Cell Biology]] at [[Yale University]] School of Medicine. He is also an Investigator at [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]. De Camilli completed his M.D. degree from the [[University of Milan]] in Italy in 1972. He then went to the United States and did his postdoctoral studies at [[Yale University]] with [[Paul Greengard]].<ref name=HHMI>{{cite web|title=Pietro De Camilli, MD|url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/pietro-de-camilli|website=HHMI|publisher=HHMI|access-date=4 August 2015}}</ref><ref name="PNAS bio">{{cite journal|last1=Bundesen|first1=L.|title=Biography of Pietro De Camilli|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=24 May 2004|volume=101|issue=22|pages=8259–8261|doi=10.1073/pnas.0403132101|pmc=420381|pmid=15159529|doi-access=free}}</ref>

De Camilli is known for contributions that has been to demonstrate the crucial role of protein-lipid interactions and phosphoinositide metabolism in the control of membrane traffic at the synapse.<ref name="HHMI Article">{{cite news|title=Membrane Traffic in Neuronal Function|url=https://www.hhmi.org/research/membrane-traffic-neuronal-function|date=3 July 2014|access-date=4 August 2015|agency=HHMI|publisher=HHMI|archive-date=26 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626104809/http://www.hhmi.org/research/membrane-traffic-neuronal-function|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He has received several awards and honors for his work. He was elected to the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 1987. In 2001, he was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] and to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 1990 he received the {{ill|Max-Planck-Forschungspreis|de}} together with Reinhard Jahn (at this time at the [[Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry]]).<ref name="PNAS bio" /> In 2019 he was awarded the [[Ernst Jung Gold Medal for Medicine]] for lifetime achievement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jung-stiftung.de/en/the-awards-ernst-jung-gold-medal-for-medicine-2019-prof-de-camilli-2/|title=Laureate PROF. PIETRO DE CAMILLI, M.D.|publisher=Ernst Jung Foundation|access-date=1 October 2019|archive-date=1 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001195732/https://jung-stiftung.de/en/the-awards-ernst-jung-gold-medal-for-medicine-2019-prof-de-camilli-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
